parts.text:

Explain why there is an increase in conductivity from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Al}$ and why $\text{P}$, $\text{S}$ and $\text{Cl}$ are non-conductors of electricity.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation, including state symbols, to represent the **third** ionisation energy of argon.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The differences in the values for third ionisation energy shown in Fig. 1.2 are due to differences in the strength of attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron of each ion.

State **two** factors that affect the strength of attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Use Fig. 1.2 to suggest the most significant factor that determines the size of attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text:
In the third ionisation energy of argon, the ion produced has the electronic configuration $1\text{s}^2 2\text{s}^2 2\text{p}^6 3\text{s}^2 3\text{p}^3$.

Complete Fig. 1.3 to show the arrangement of electrons in the orbitals of this ion.
